claims.text: The Congressional Research Service's intelligence-community leadership roster records the office and the date as 'Director of the National Reconnaissance Office (D/NRO) Betty J. Sapp (sworn in July 6, 2012)', and gives Christopher Scolese as 'nominated, February 7, 2019' in the same row.

The same table gives the appointment authority for the post she held: '50 U.S.C. 3041(b)(2)(B) DOD Secretary needs DNI to concur with the recommendation to the President; and 50 U.S.C. 3602(a)(2), Director is appointment by the President, Senate confirmed; then pursuant to S.Res. 470, Senate confirmed (SSCI and SASC).'

label: Betty J. Sapp
narrative: Director of the National Reconnaissance Office, sworn in 6 July 2012 and still named in post when the Congressional Research Service last revised its intelligence-community leadership roster in March 2019, by which time a successor had been nominated. The board carries the NRO as its working precedent for an agency whose existence was itself classified for thirty-one years, and until now carried no personnel for it at all. The Area 52 corpus places her earlier at Wright-Patterson, at CIA from 1997 and in a Deputy Under Secretary of Defense post from 2007 with oversight of the Military Intelligence Program; none of that is in any record opened here, because nro.gov refuses this environment, and it is recorded as a gap rather than as a claim.
